groups.title: Republic and Society
groups.context: Shared institutions. Pompidou remains the historical starting president.

groups.title: UDR: Gaullist Government
groups.context: Pompidou and Chaban-Delmas. UDR becomes RPR only through actual dated party identity changes.

groups.title: Independent Republicans
groups.context: Giscard leads a distinct liberal conservative programme. Governing requires native slot 2, not coalition membership.

groups.title: Democratic Centre
groups.context: CD governs this branch. CDP is a real separate coalition current, represented by an internal cooperation choice until a registry change is approved.

groups.title: Radical Republicans
groups.context: The unified Radical Party exists in January 1970. Left-radical separation is a later political choice, not a starting party.

groups.title: Socialist Party
groups.context: PS exists under Alain Savary in 1970. CIR and the 1971 Epinay refoundation belong to its development, not an invented 1970 Mitterrand PS presidency.

groups.title: French Communist Party
groups.context: PCF under Rochet, with Marchais rising. Eurocommunist and orthodox options are real internal tensions, not separate invented mass parties.

groups.title: Unified Socialist Party
groups.context: PSU has a distinct anti-authoritarian socialist programme. Autogestion is developed as a policy option, not claimed as its settled January 1970 doctrine.

groups.title: Political Ecology
groups.context: A future ecological governing alternative, grounded in Dumont 1974 and later movements. Not a mass governing party in January 1970.

groups.title: Shopkeepers and the National Right
groups.context: CID is the actual 1970 slot identity. FN requires its real foundation on 5 October 1972 and an alternate-history accession. Separate receipts prevent CID policies becoming FN rewards automatically.

groups.title: Industry, Regions and Energy
groups.context: Shared national assets and persistent reforms. No date barrier except technology, survey and real external crisis conditions.

groups.title: Independent Defence
groups.context: Shared armed forces. Real platforms, nuclear stockpiles and technology are never awarded by a ceremonial focus.

groups.title: Partnerships by Consent
groups.context: Distinct French proposal focuses. Named recipients receive Accept and Decline decisions. All terms stay inspectable while locked.

groups.title: Gaullist NATO Strategy
groups.context: A UDR sub-tree. France remains a NATO treaty member outside integrated military command. The three strategies prioritise different funded capabilities and partnerships, not three fictional accession statuses.

nodes.title: A State Within Reach
nodes.description: Prefects and central ministries possess formidable authority. A practical administrative reform can shorten the distance between citizens and public services.

nodes.title: Executive Safeguards
nodes.description: Defend the presidential mandate while placing the emergency machinery of the Fifth Republic on a clearer statutory footing.

nodes.title: Parliamentary Checks
nodes.description: Strengthen scrutiny of ministers and public appointments without returning France to the unstable cabinet arithmetic of the Fourth Republic.

nodes.title: Social Settlement
nodes.description: Bring employers and unions into regular national bargaining. Wage assurances must be matched by investment and reliable public financing.

nodes.title: Statutory Labour Pact
nodes.description: Legislate minimum protections and clear strike procedures. National standards can secure continuity, but imposed terms risk weakening workplace consent.

nodes.title: Historical Recognition
nodes.description: Recognise the distinct experiences of veterans, harkis, repatriates and Algerian families. Public recognition commits the state to support as well as remembrance.

nodes.title: Republican Amnesty
nodes.description: Extend the logic of the late-1960s amnesties to close domestic conflicts over Algeria. Reconciliation with former opponents leaves other claims unresolved.

nodes.title: Civic Settlement
nodes.description: Give public institutions a durable basis for integration and remembrance, without requiring citizens to share a single account of the end of empire.

nodes.title: Progress Contract
nodes.description: Chaban-Delmas proposes to replace entrenched confrontation with negotiated progress in public enterprises. The presidency must decide how far that opening should go.

nodes.title: The Hague Opening
nodes.description: Use the opening achieved at The Hague to pursue enlargement and practical European cooperation, while preserving a French voice within it.

nodes.title: Gaullist Majority
nodes.description: Rebuild the governing movement around a social and industrial programme that can outlast its founding president.

nodes.title: Modern Liberal State
nodes.description: Giscardian reform links administrative competence to private initiative. Support for enterprise requires visible restraints on public privilege.

nodes.title: A Sound Franc
nodes.description: Defend monetary credibility through tighter public demand and a consistent budget. Investors gain confidence while domestic expansion slows.

nodes.title: Modernisation Credit
nodes.description: Direct cheaper credit toward modern equipment and housing. Faster construction brings a continuing subsidy bill and a looser claim on fiscal restraint.

nodes.title: Atlantic Trade

nodes.title: European Market
nodes.description: Build a European market large enough for competitive French firms. The benefits of scale require costly adjustment for sheltered producers.

nodes.title: Social Market

nodes.title: Regional Councils

nodes.title: Centrist Covenant

nodes.title: American Challenge

nodes.title: Republican Left

nodes.title: France and NATO
nodes.description: France remains bound by the Atlantic Treaty after the 1966 command withdrawal. Pompidou can reaffirm national discretion, deepen conditional military cooperation or concentrate on a European contribution to the Alliance. None of these choices transfers authority over the French deterrent.
nodes.basis: NATO historical account; Ailleret-Lemnitzer exchange of letters, 1967.
nodes.nato_policy: Treaty membership retained; national command and nuclear decision remain French.

nodes.title: National Nuclear Veto
nodes.description: Finance an independent assessment and decision system for the force de frappe. National authority strengthens the Gaullist mandate while France bears the full equipment-support burden of its separate capability.
nodes.basis: Gaullist national nuclear authority. The cost modifier changes the recurring MD equipment bill, not factory IC.
nodes.nato_policy: Treaty membership retained; national command and nuclear decision remain French.

nodes.title: Nuclear Consultation
nodes.description: Consult allies about deterrence and escalation while reserving the final decision to France. Better understanding of allied doctrine does not entail NPG membership, nuclear sharing or an allied veto over French weapons.
nodes.basis: NATO consultation and France national-command reservations; Ottawa 1974 as a later precedent, not a treaty already signed in 1970.
nodes.nato_policy: Treaty membership retained; national command and nuclear decision remain French.

nodes.title: An Independent Ally
nodes.description: Keep Atlantic political solidarity while concentrating discretionary defence funds on capabilities controlled and sustained by France. A stronger independent position reduces outside leverage but duplicates part of the equipment-support establishment.
nodes.basis: Historical Gaullist position: treaty solidarity and national command. Exclusive choice allocates an additional programme budget, not a legal ban on other cooperation.
nodes.nato_policy: Treaty membership retained; national command and nuclear decision remain French.

nodes.title: Selective Cooperation

nodes.title: A European Pillar

offer.acceptance_transaction: Recheck consent, country and programme conditions, own GDP initialisation and all asset feasibility before mutation. Calculate each setup from its own payer current GDP. Charge and grant both sides atomically once; add each state slot before its building and record one-time research, doctrine, experience and faction awards. offer.cost_basis: Each signatory own current gdp_total at acceptance; annual programme share recalculated from each own GDP / 52 weekly. No French GDP reuse for the recipient.
offer.asset_execution: Acceptance rechecks ownership, control and capacity for each promised asset on both sides before paying either side. One-time assets/slots share the signed transaction receipt; restoration never repeats them.
offer.payment_contract: French and recipient setup charges use separate own-country current GDP bases at acceptance; weekly annual-GDP appropriations use each own current GDP / 52. One atomic once-only transaction, no fixed-price building charge or Treasury-balance gate.

starting_spirits.title: The Fifth Republic
starting_spirits.description: Pompidou inherits a powerful presidency and a large Gaullist majority. Administrative concentration gives the executive room to act while narrowing parliamentary and local influence.
starting_spirits.remedy: Executive Safeguards or Parliamentary Checks replaces this spirit.

starting_spirits.title: The Unfinished Settlement of Grenelle
starting_spirits.description: The wage settlement ended a national confrontation without resolving disputes over management, representation and the distribution of growth.
starting_spirits.remedy: A shared negotiated or statutory settlement replaces this spirit; party spending alone does not erase it.

starting_spirits.title: Uneven Modernisation
starting_spirits.description: Competitive firms and ambitious public projects coexist with crowded cities, remote rural communities and vulnerable industrial districts.
starting_spirits.remedy: Regional Connections and an industrial strategy remove the starting imbalance.

starting_spirits.title: Oil-Intensive Growth
starting_spirits.description: Cheap imported oil sustains transport and industry. High demand leaves national prosperity exposed to supply disputes, price changes and the exchange rate.
starting_spirits.remedy: The selected energy programme reduces the burden; no automatic 1973 shock is applied in 1970.

starting_spirits.title: A Narrow Route to Expertise
starting_spirits.description: Elite schools and national laboratories support advanced science, while technical training and mass university provision struggle to keep pace.
starting_spirits.remedy: Technical Colleges or Mass Universities replaces this spirit with its stated outcome.

starting_spirits.title: The Price of Independence
starting_spirits.description: The national deterrent and an independent procurement system preserve strategic freedom while drawing resources from conventional forces and civilian investment.
starting_spirits.remedy: The defence chapter replaces this inherited strategic settlement, preserving actual native nuclear running costs.

starting_spirits.title: The Postcolonial Settlement
starting_spirits.description: Repatriation, migrant housing and competing memories of Algeria burden public trust. Overseas commitments also test the reach of a centralised state.
starting_spirits.remedy: Housing and Rights plus either Historical Recognition or Republican Amnesty replaces this spirit.

starting_spirits.title: After the 1969 Devaluation
starting_spirits.description: The franc adjustment supports export orders, while the credit restraint used to stabilise demand weighs on construction and domestic investment.
starting_spirits.remedy: Temporary opening condition: ends after 270 days, representing the easing of 1970 restrictions; never re-applied.

rules.party_visibility: All branches always visible; exact native ruling-party requirements gate execution and programme activation.
rules.party_lifecycle: Earned party modifier deltas detach when the party leaves and return on re-entry. Monetary transactions, assets, XP and research never replay. Shared institutions and national assets persist.
rules.offers: A French focus sends a fixed-partner recipient-owned Accept/Decline decision. No benefit before acceptance. Both signatories pay once on acceptance. Seven proposal days per focus cost unit.
rules.treaty_lifecycle: Signed agreements have no expiry. Both countries must exist, remain at peace with one another, and impose neither native embargo nor any diplomatic, financial, economic or military Imperia sanction in either direction. Suspend both spirits and their running streams while invalid; restore both without repeating setup or finite awards. Actual active parent spirits are required for dependent agreements.
rules.family_limit: One signed agreement per named family. An exclusive focus choice remains a sovereign French policy choice even after refusal; a recipient can always decline. Reissues preserve the fixed partner and require fresh consent.
rules.weekly: Standing programme budgets are annual percentages of each payer own current gdp_total, divided by 52 and recalculated in the native weekly expense stream. Store share literals with at most five fractional digits and divide by integer 52. Expense multipliers change the corresponding existing weekly bill. All percentages are game-balance proposals, not reconstructed historical budgets.
rules.assets: One extra shared slot per building level in the same state, before construction, under a single one-time guard. Actual ownership, control and native capacity checked separately. No automatic uranium production or free technology.
rules.politics: Succession and elections remain native. No automatic coup, forced recipient government, annexation or treaty acceptance. CIR/CDP representation needs historical registry refinement before implementation.
rules.preview: External concept using native art; routing/font/frames are approximations. This is not a running-game screenshot.
rules.treasury: Every one-time Treasury charge is a signed percentage of the payer own current annual gdp_total at the actual payment. Bilateral signatories use separate GDP bases in their own country scopes. The percentage is agreed; the amount updates with GDP. Previews never execute costs. No Treasury-balance availability or delivery gate is added. GDP availability is an internal initialisation guard, never a fixed-price fallback.
rules.nato_lifecycle: NATO-specific agreements additionally require NATO_member on both signatories. Losing membership suspends both spirits and weekly streams while preserving signatures; return restores them without setup, XP or research replay. Membership itself is never restored by this subsystem. Government-bound NATO programme modifiers require current UDR rule, NATO_member and any actual active parent agreement. Signed bilateral treaties do not require UDR to remain in government.

nato.membership: All paths require and retain NATO_member. No NATO_join or NATO_leave call is proposed.
nato.nuclear: Independent nuclear authority remains in every path; consultation grants neither NPG membership nor nuclear sharing.
nato.parent_activation: Cooperation-derived party programmes require both current UDR government and the actual active parent agreement. Treaties survive government change; no finite award replays.
nato.baseline: Existing 1967 arrangements remain historical starting context; offers fund additional activity, not retroactive consent for signed agreements.
